site_name: Microsoft West Des Moines data center campus, 550 SE White Crane Rd (permit name: Willow Creek and Ginger East Data Centers)
notes: Utility is LOW confidence and indirect: no utility, commission or operator document naming the provider for this address was found. The only support is Bloomberg reporting (June 2022, republished by Data Center Knowledge) that Microsoft petitioned the Iowa Utilities Board as part of the 'tech-customer coalition' in MidAmerican's Wind PRIME case, which implies Microsoft's Iowa data centers (all in West Des Moines) are MidAmerican customers. MidAmerican's own data-center pages name no customers. Treat as a hypothesis. Energized year NOT FOUND for this campus. Context only: Microsoft says its first West Des Moines datacenter opened in 2012 and that it planned to open a fourth and fifth campus by end of 2023 (https://news.microsoft.com/source/features/ai/west-des-moines-iowa-ai-supercomputer/); which campus 'Willow Creek' is was not established. Load in 2025 NOT FOUND. planned_full_buildout_mw 444 is the MISO public large-load list (updated Dec 6 2024) row 'Microsoft (Project Ginger East), West Des Moines, IA, 444 MW', planned date 2025-2027; it covers Ginger East only (Willow Creek is not listed separately) and MISO labels the list as compiled from public announcements, not for planning reliance. County from the Census geocoder at the worklist coordinates.

site_name: Microsoft Project Osmium data center campus, 5855 SW Kerry St, West Des Moines
load_basis: MISO public large-load list (updated Dec 6 2024): 'Microsoft (Project Osmium), West Des Moines, IA, 150 MW', planned date 2025. Announced load compiled from public information, not a metered or operator-stated figure.
notes: Utility is LOW confidence and indirect: same basis as the other West Des Moines campus (Bloomberg/Data Center Knowledge, June 2022: Microsoft joined the 'tech-customer coalition' before the Iowa Utilities Board in MidAmerican's Wind PRIME case). No utility, commission or operator document naming the provider for this site was found; Clarke Electric Coop and Interstate Power & Light were not ruled out by a document. Year: the Greater Des Moines Partnership's 2021 data-center flier says of Microsoft's third West Des Moines campus 'the first two buildings on this campus were constructed in 2020', with a third building to break ground June 2021. That is a construction date, not a stated commercial-operation date, so 2020 is low confidence (first operation could be 2021). Identification of the 'third campus' with Osmium rests on the 2016 trade-press description of the third campus as south of Maffitt Reservoir on the Warren/Madison county line (https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/hyperscalers/microsoft-still-mum-on-huge-new-iowa-project). Our permit-based guess of 2024 looks late. planned_full_buildout_mw repeats the same MISO 150 MW figure because no separate full-buildout number from an acceptable source was found. County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: Amazon (AWS) Dublin campus building CMH051, Houchard Rd & Dublin Plain City Rd (SR 161), Washington Township
operator: Amazon (Amazon Data Services, Inc., formerly Vadata)
notes: Utility: the joint application of Amazon Data Services and Ohio Power Company in PUCO Case No. 23-0858-EL-AEC (public redacted version, copy hosted by NBC4) states ADS operates data centers 'in AEP Ohio's territory across [redacted] data center campuses in Hilliard, Dublin, and New Albany'. Confidence is medium rather than high because the filing does not give street addresses; tying this Houchard Rd/SR 161 building to the Dublin campus is an inference from location (those were the only three existing campuses). Arrangement: the existing campuses were under a PUCO-approved economic development arrangement (Case No. 17-1827-EL-AEC, approved 2018); the 2023 filing says ADS 'voluntarily elected to exit this prior reasonable rate arrangement effective May 31, 2023'. So this site was special-contract service from 2018 to May 2023 and tariff service after; 'retail' reflects 2025 status. The 2023 arrangement applies to new campuses. No rate terms were recorded. Year: the City of Dublin economic development office reported on Oct 18 2016 that Amazon's Hilliard, Dublin and New Albany data centers were 'up and running'. That dates the Dublin campus's first building; the CMH051 building itself (first generator permit 2020) is probably a later addition, year not found. Load NOT FOUND (MW figures are redacted in the PUCO filing). County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: JPMorgan Chase Orangeburg data center campus (75 3rd Ave / 140 Old Orangeburg Rd, former Rockland Psychiatric Center land)
notes: Utility: News 12 (Apr 2026) reports Orange and Rockland Utilities said it 'is reviewing the expansion's impact on the grid' for the second building on JPMorgan's existing Orangeburg campus. That names O&R as the utility for the campus; no tariff or contract detail was found. The reporting gives the campus address as 140 Old Orangeburg Road on the former Rockland Psychiatric Center property; I am treating 75 3rd Ave as the same campus but did not find a document equating the two addresses. Energized year NOT FOUND: Data Center Knowledge (Feb 8 2017) has JPMorgan still bidding for the 60-acre site, and New York Focus/Route Fifty (Apr 2026) dates the first Rockland IDA deal to 2017, so the first building opened after 2017; no source gives the opening year. Load NOT FOUND for the existing building or the expansion (expansion completion expected 2028). County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: QTS Phoenix 2 campus, DC1, 1200 N 40th St, Phoenix
notes: Utility: AZ Big Media (May 25 2020), describing QTS's second Phoenix site at McDowell Rd between 37th and 40th streets, says 'QTS is working with SRP on locating a power substation on the property' sized for two data center buildings. That is a pre-construction statement, so medium confidence; no SRP or QTS document confirming the energized service was found, and QTS's campus page names no utility. Energized year NOT FOUND from an acceptable source (the 2020 article has earthwork starting early 2020 and vertical construction hoped for by end of 2020). Load in 2025 NOT FOUND: a QTS DC1 data sheet reported to list 42 MW critical could not be opened (the old URL redirects to a 404), so it is not recorded. planned_full_buildout_mw 210 is QTS's own Phoenix 2 page: '210 MW+' critical campus capacity across five buildings (DC1 at 1200 N 40th St through DC5 at 1500). County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: Amazon data center campus, 77860 Bombing Range Rd, Boardman
notes: Utility: The Oregonian (Apr 11 2023, republished by the La Grande Observer) reports Amazon 'has started working with the local power utility, Umatilla Electric Cooperative' on power supply for its data centers near Boardman and Hermiston, and refers to Amazon's wholesale power contracts. That names UEC as the delivering utility for Amazon's Boardman-area data centers as a group; no source naming this specific address was found, so confidence is medium, not high. service_arrangement is set to special_contract on the strength of that article's description of a negotiated supply-choice deal between Amazon and UEC; the contract itself is not public and this label should be treated as medium confidence. UEC's own project pages (umatillaelectric.com/about-us/news-events-updates/projects/) list Boardman-area substations built for 'member growth' but never name Amazon. BPA is the transmission provider and wholesale supplier to UEC, not the retail deliverer. Energized year NOT FOUND. The Hermiston Herald (Aug 22 2023) says 'Another center campus is under construction along Bombing Range Road' without naming the operator (https://hermistonherald.com/2023/08/22/decision-on-boardman-data-center-delayed-by-new-testimony/); if that is this campus, first operation was 2024 or later, consistent with but not confirming our 2024 guess. Load NOT FOUND. County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: Digital Realty (former DuPont Fabros Technology) Ashburn Corporate Center campus, 44490 Chilum Place, Ashburn
operator: Digital Realty (acquired DuPont Fabros Technology in 2017)
notes: Utility NOT FOUND in a citable source: DuPont Fabros's 10-K filings (FY2007 and FY2016 read in full or nearly so) refer only to 'local utilities' and never name the provider, and Digital Realty's facility pages name none. Our Dominion (Virginia Electric & Power) assignment is the only mapped candidate and is very likely right, but it remains a territory-map inference, so the field is left null. Year: DuPont Fabros's FY2016 10-K lists its Ashburn buildings as ACC2 (built 2001, renovated 2005, 10.4 MW critical load), ACC3 (2001/2006, 13.9 MW), ACC4 (2007, 36.4 MW), ACC5 (2009-2010, 36.4 MW) and ACC6 (2011-2013, 26.0 MW). 2005 is the first DFT data center on this campus (ACC2) and matches the 2005 first generator permit, but no filing gives street addresses, so which building sits at 44490 Chilum Place is not established (Digital Realty today lists ACC4 at 44480 Hastings Dr, ACC5 at 44521 Hastings Dr and ACC6 at 44461 Chilum Pl, and no longer lists ACC2 or ACC3). Low confidence for that reason. Load left null because the building is not identified; the per-building critical loads above are the candidates, and the five together total 123.1 MW, which would double count if other rows of this permit cover the other buildings. County from the Census geocoder.

site_name: Microsoft Leesburg data center campus (IAD01-04), Compass Creek, 19935 Sycolin Rd / 19515 Compass Creek Pkwy
notes: Utility: reporting on Virginia DEQ's 2026 consent order says Microsoft's Leesburg data center ran on its backup generators for days in mid-2025 after a failure at the nearby Cochran Mill electrical substation; WJLA (Sep 15 2026, fetched) names the substation and gives the facility address as 19515 Compass Creek Parkway. The statement that the Cochran Mill substation belongs to Northern Virginia Electric Cooperative comes from Virginia Business (https://virginiabusiness.com/deq-microsoft-2-5m-penalties-leesburg-data-center/) and Northern Virginia Magazine as surfaced in search results; both pages refused direct fetch (403), as did DEQ's order and permit pages, so I did not read that sentence on the page myself. Medium confidence on that basis. The same reporting says Microsoft has since added a dual-feed system. Dominion (the other mapped candidate) supplies NOVEC at transmission level but is not indicated as the retail provider. I am treating 19935 Sycolin Rd (the permit address) and 19515 Compass Creek Pkwy as the same campus; the permit name IAD01-02-03-04 matches the building names in local reporting. Energized year left null: the Blue Ridge Leader (Nov 29 2023) says the first two Microsoft buildings, IAD01-1 and IAD01-2, 'were built between 2019-2021' (https://blueridgeleader.com/?p=20845), which brackets but does not fix the first year of operation (our guess is 2021). Load NOT FOUND. County from the Census geocoder.
